I've attached the same NO2 air pollution data for 33 London boroughs (Q1 2021) and the same borough adjacency list.

This time, I want specific individual boroughs (not an overall city-wide pattern) that fall into one of these two categories:
- HOT SPOT: a borough with a high NO2 air pollution that is ALSO surrounded by other high-NO2 air pollution neighboring boroughs
- COLD SPOT: a borough with a low NO2 air pollution that is ALSO surrounded by other low-NO2 air pollution neighboring boroughs

Look at each borough together with its neighbors from the adjacency list, and identify any that qualify. Explain your reasoning, including a computed value for each borough you name. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. For implementation including statistical method such as Moran's I, directly use only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HH for hot spot and LL for cold spot, and including a computed value for each:

Thought: First, load the data, drop boroughs with missing NO₂, build a symmetric adjacency list, and compute each borough’s local Moran’s I.  
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv("chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_no2_Q1_2021.csv")
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop NaNs
df = df.dropna(subset=["value"]).reset_index(drop=True)
# Global mean and variance denominator S2
x = df["value"].values
mean_x = x.mean()
S2 = ((x - mean_x)**2).sum() / len(x)

# Build adjacency dict (only among boroughs in df)
boroughs = set(df["borough"])
adjacency = {b: set() for b in boroughs}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, nb = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    if b in boroughs and nb in boroughs:
        adjacency[b].add(nb)
        adjacency[nb].add(b)

# Compute local Moran's I
local_I = {}
for b in df["borough"]:
    xi = df.loc[df["borough"] == b, "value"].iloc[0]
    neighbors = adjacency[b]
    if len(neighbors) == 0:
        local_I[b] = np.nan
        continue
    xj = df.set_index("borough").loc[list(neighbors), "value"].values
    local_I[b] = (xi - mean_x) * ((xj - mean_x).sum()) / S2

# Output
for b, Ii in local_I.items():
    print(f"{b}: I = {Ii:.4f}")
print("mean_x:", mean_x, "S2:", S2)
```

Thought: Compute for each borough its NO₂, neighbor-average NO₂, and local I, then pick ones where both borough and neighbors are above the city mean (hot spots) or both below (cold spots).  
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data and adjacency
df = pd.read_csv("chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_no2_Q1_2021.csv").dropna(subset=["value"])
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# City mean and S2
values = df["value"].values
mean_x = values.mean()
S2 = ((values - mean_x)**2).sum() / len(values)

# Build adjacency dict
boroughs = set(df["borough"])
adjacency = {b: set() for b in boroughs}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, nb = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    if b in boroughs and nb in boroughs:
        adjacency[b].add(nb)
        adjacency[nb].add(b)

# Compute stats
records = []
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    b = row["borough"]
    xi = row["value"]
    neighbors = list(adjacency[b])
    if not neighbors:
        continue
    xj = df.set_index("borough").loc[neighbors, "value"].values
    neighbor_mean = xj.mean()
    Ii = (xi - mean_x) * (xj - mean_x).sum() / S2
    records.append((b, xi, neighbor_mean, Ii))

stats = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=["borough","xi","neighbor_mean","local_I"])
print("City mean NO2:", mean_x)
# Identify hot and cold spots
hot = stats[(stats["xi"] > mean_x) & (stats["neighbor_mean"] > mean_x)]
cold = stats[(stats["xi"] < mean_x) & (stats["neighbor_mean"] < mean_x)]
print("Hot spot candidates:")
print(hot)
print("Cold spot candidates:")
print(cold)
```
